title: Knob queue classifier and SLA-aware routing prototype
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a lightweight prototype classifier to automatically route optimization and advisory requests (batching/caching knobs, quantization profiles, routing policies) into prioritized queues based on customer SLA, cost-sensitivity, and operational complexity. Deliverables: 1) classifier model + feature spec, 2) routing rules and confidence thresholds, 3) fallback/human-review path, 4) telemetry to measure precision and SLA outcomes. Acceptance criteria: routing precision >= 75% for top-3 lanes on pilot traffic, automated routing reduces manual triage time by >= 40% in pilot, and prototype publishes decision logs to the Optimization Console dashboard.
comments: 2026-03-13 | Asha Patel: Kickoff — scoped prototype to cover three lanes: self-serve knobby recommendations, concierge (solutions engineering assisted), and enterprise escalation (SLA or compliance). We will use historical advisory ticket metadata and customer signals (tier, recent latency alerts, model family, request verbatim) to train a classifier. Initial scope excludes deep model-specific quantization tuning — those stay human-reviewed.

2026-03-13 | Miguel Ortega: Engineering alignment — Eng will expose a lightweight /classify endpoint in the intake service. Plan to use a gradient-boosted tree (XGBoost) using feature bag from Zendesk/Intake form + usage metrics from Console. Low-confidence results (prob < 0.6) route to human queue. Need data schema and PIIs scrubbed before model training.

2026-03-13 | Priya Menon (Optimization): Feature notes — add signals: 'observed token distribution', 'median latency over 24h', 'burstiness score', 'has_private_deployment_flag'. Early experiments show 'customer_tier' and 'latency_sensitivity' are strongest predictors of concierge/enterprise lanes.

2026-03-14 | Miguel Ortega: Prototype PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/opt-orchestrator/pull/342. This includes training pipeline, model export, and a mock classifier service. Initial test run on 3k labeled tickets: precision@1 = 0.72, recall@1 = 0.68. Comments on trade-offs in PR about skewed classes and overfitting to large-enterprise language patterns.

2026-03-14 | Security (Liam Chen): Reviewed data handling notes — no raw customer prompts in training set; only metadata and redacted tags. Confirmed KMS usage for model artifact encryption. Recommended a short privacy review before pilot rollout.

2026-03-14 | Asha Patel: Decision log — move forward with prototype pilot for two customer segments (Enterprise customers with SLA clauses and high-usage startups). Success metrics: classification precision >= 0.75, manual triage time reduction >= 40%, false-negative enterprise-escalations <= 2/week. If prototype fails, fall back to rule-based routing and revisit feature set.

2026-03-14 | Product Analytics (E. Rivera): Instrumentation checklist — log classifier input features, decision latency, confidence score, downstream SLA outcome tags (missed SLA, cost-savings recommendation accepted). Create dashboard: /dashboards/optimization-routing-prototype.

2026-03-14 | Next steps assigned: 1) Eng to wire /classify endpoint and decision logs (ENG-1842), 2) Data team to deliver labeled dataset slice and feature-engineering script, 3) PM to coordinate pilot customers and runbook for manual override steps. Target pilot date: 2026-03-28.
